subject: Re: Nimbus - realtime throughput spike & websocket timeouts
messages:
From: Alicia Ruiz <alicia.ruiz@nimbushealth.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Carlos Vega <c.vega@nimbushealth.com>
Date: 2027-12-26T17:12:00Z
Subject: Realtime feed: elevated latency and WS timeouts

David —

We saw a sustained spike in end-to-end latency and an uptick in 502/504 errors on our realtime endpoint between 02:00–03:30 PT this morning. Clients using the websocket ingestion experienced disconnects and several streams reported truncated outputs (clients reporting missing final chunks). The issue correlates with our heaviest batch of nightly inference jobs.

Attached are the error logs and a packet capture from one affected instance. Key observations from our side:
- Median p99 latency jumped from ~120ms to ~2.1s for a 45-minute window
- Websocket clients saw abrupt disconnects and "connection reset by peer" messages
- Throughput (requests/sec) was within expected range but token-emission stalls appeared (partial chunks)

This is impacting a set of scheduled workflows tomorrow morning; we need an immediate mitigation and a timeline for root cause/patch.

Thanks,
Alicia Ruiz
Head of Platform Integrations
Nimbus Health

Attachments: nimbus_error_log_20271226.txt, packet-trace-peak.pcap

Alicia —

Thanks for the signal and the artifacts. I'm pulling Hannah and our support lead Vanessa into the thread so we can triage. Immediate asks while we investigate:
1) Can you confirm if clients that saw truncated outputs retried automatically or logged partial events?
2) If possible, keep one affected client running and forward live logs to ops@nimbushealth.com — that will help correlate.

Short-term mitigations we can apply from our side right away (pending your approval):
- Route your traffic to our warm standby region to reduce burst pressure (minor latency delta)
- Temporarily lower concurrency ceiling for your API key to reduce simultaneous KV/cache pressure
- Enable stream chunk acknowledgements (server-side) to force smaller frame sizes

Vanessa/Hannah: can you confirm which config flips are lowest-risk to apply now? I want to be explicit in the response to Nimbus.

—David
Director, Customer Reliability

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.inference.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.inference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Alicia Ruiz <alicia.ruiz@nimbushealth.com>
Date: 2027-12-26T21:10:00Z
Subject: Re: Realtime feed: elevated latency and WS timeouts

David/Vanessa/Alicia —

Preliminary engineering notes after an initial pass on the logs and the pcap:
- Root-cause hypothesis: proxy buffer exhaustion + chunked transfer timeouts. During the peak, several large responses with high token emission rates accumulated behind the proxy; the proxy started dropping/closing idle chunked connections when its output buffer exceeded soft limits. That behavior surfaced as truncated final chunks and abrupt WS disconnects.
- Correlated event: a rolling kernel update on a subset of serving hosts reduced the effective socket buffer by default (sysctl change), which amplified buffer pressure under this burst pattern.

Short-term mitigations (can be implemented within 1–3 hours with a low-risk rollout):
1) Increase proxy output buffer and keepalive timeout for Nimbus's route (config flip; reversible). Expected impact: reduces chunk drops immediately.
2) Throttle per-connection token emission rate (server-side limiter) to smooth peaks. Expected impact: avoids buffer amplification but may increase end-to-end latency by ~150–300ms p99.
3) Route traffic to warm-standby region for the next 6 hours while we patch configs (adds ~80ms median latency but removes the stressed hosts).

Medium-term fixes (2–3 weeks):
- Adaptive batching: tune batch sizes based on token distribution to avoid sudden large responses
- KV cache eviction tuning: preferentially keep small-prefix caches hot for streaming workloads
- Revert/standardize socket buffer sysctl across the fleet and add a canary before kernel rollouts

I've attached a short diagnostic bundle (proxy-metrics-20271226.csv) and the packet-trace. I'll initiate a canary for the proxy buffer increase immediately upon approval.

—Hannah
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Attachments: proxy-metrics-20271226.csv, packet-trace-peak.pcap

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.inference.com>

Date: 2027-12-27T14:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Nimbus - realtime throughput spike & websocket timeouts

Team —

Executive summary for Nimbus and internal stakeholders:
- Impact: Intermittent websocket disconnects and truncated streaming outputs during a 90-minute peak window; p99 latency elevated to ~2s; no confirmed data loss yet (customers reported partial chunks, we are treating as potential loss).
- Immediate action (next 1–3 hours):
  1) Approve proxy output buffer increase (canary now, fleetwide in 6 hours if green).
  2) Enable per-connection token emission throttle for their API key for 6 hours.
  3) Optional: route traffic to warm-standby region (Nimbus approval required) — estimated added latency +80ms, but avoids the affected hosts.
- ETA: we can have the canary deployed in ~45 minutes; if green, we will expand to their fleet in 6 hours. Full remediation plan (adaptive batching, sysctl rollbacks) targeted for 2–3 weeks.
- Business ask: Markus, please confirm the communication and whether a proactive credit is required to mitigate renewal risk for D-9834. Vanessa, I'll prepare a 1-page customer-facing summary (including mitigation steps and timeline) and circulate in the next 30 minutes.

Alicia — can you confirm whether Nimbus wants us to route to standby region while we run the canary? If yes, we'll schedule the cutover within the hour.

Thanks,
David
